messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: high CPU + OOM on tokenizer pods in us-west-2 cluster. 5 pod restarts in last 7m, node flaps detected. Impacting /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints.

alex (oncall): acked. I'm on it. assigning triage. @maria can you pull node metrics and see if it's a single machine or a coord issue?

maria (infra): looking at node metrics now. appears to be two nodes in the pool cycling to NotReady around 02:04 and 02:09 UTC. CPU at 98% on kube-node-12 and 94% on kube-node-15.

sanjay (runtime): logs from tokenizer pods show repeated "fatal: runtime: out of memory" and `SIGKILL` in the tokenization worker. Also seeing CUDA driver errors for a subset of pods: `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` but that might be a red herring from mixed workload.

alex (oncall): ok primary hypothesis: tokenizer/prompt preprocessing hot loop eating CPU, leading kubelet eviction and node flaps. Begin immediate mitigation: 1) scale down tokenizer replicas, 2) cordon + drain the flapping nodes, 3) rate-limit incoming requests at the ingress for affected routes.

mike (sre): I'm scaling tokenizer deployment to 2 replicas from 8 to stop the immediate churn: `kubectl scale deploy/tokenizer --replicas=2 -n inference`

opsbot: deploy token:scale initiated by mike at 2026-03-15T02:11:03Z

irina (cs): customers: three enterprise tenants reporting increased 500s. CS ticket #INC-3981 opened. ETA for mitigation? they asked for a status note.

alex (oncall): tell them we're investigating a tokenizer CPU issue causing pod restarts, mitigation in progress, will update in 15m.

maria (infra): cordoning kube-node-12 and draining. `kubectl cordon kube-node-12 && kubectl drain kube-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

sanjay (runtime): while draining, I'm attaching to a live tokenizer pod to sample stacks. attaching with `kubectl exec -it tokenizer-7b-xx -- bash` and running `py-spy top --pid 1`

sanjay (runtime): sample shows tight loop inside prompt preprocessor when processing unusually long user prompt with many repeated emojis. stack snippet: 
```
File "tokenizer.py", line 421, in preprocess
  for chunk in split_on_unicode_runs(text):
    normalize_whitespace(chunk)
```
Looks like `split_on_unicode_runs` degenerates to O(n^2) on certain inputs.

alex (oncall): that aligns. Can we patch the preprocessor to short-circuit very long single-token inputs? If not fast deploy, fallback: block huge prompt lengths at the ingress as emergency rule.

maria (infra): added an emergency ingress rule to reject body > 200k bytes with 413. rule pushed to edge at 02:22 UTC.

opsbot: edge-rule:reject-large-payloads deployed by maria.

sanjay (runtime): quick fix: rolled a runtime config to set MAX_PREPROCESS_TOKENS=10000 for tokenizer workers. rolling restart started.

alex (oncall): good. what's the customer impact now?

irina (cs): after scaling and ingress rule, error rate dropped from 18% -> 6% for affected tenants. two tenants still seeing intermittent 502s. CS will escalate for those two.

mike (sre): draining the flapping nodes completed. kube-node-12 shows kernel OOM kills in dmesg around 02:05. Suspect noise from other processes; I'll isolate and repro on a staging node.

sanjay (runtime): restarted crashed tokenizer pods, logs show preprocessor no longer spinning after config change. Memory usage stable. Also seeing fewer CUDA error lines — likely caused by severe CPU pressure earlier.

alex (oncall): create a followup ticket to rewrite split_on_unicode_runs algorithm, link to stack sample and problematic payload. Prioritize as P1 for runtime team.

sanjay (runtime): created TICKET-9872: "preprocessor degeneracy on long unicode runs -> CPU OOM" with sample payload and stack.

mike (sre): nodes are stable now. replacing drained nodes with fresh instances to avoid latent corruption. autoscaler brought new nodes up, pods redistributed.

irina (cs): sending customers a short update: mitigation applied (ingress size limit + runtime throttle). Root cause under investigation.

alex (oncall): handing off to night oncall @mike for monitoring until 06:00 UTC. I'm running post-incident checklist and drafting the incident blameless summary.

mike (sre): taking over. will monitor for 2 hours and escalate if errors > 5% sustained.

opsbot: incident created: INC-3981 (ticket-tracker) assigned to ops, runtime; severity: sev2; start_ts=1782005000

alex (oncall): timeline notes: 02:04 alert -> 02:11 initial triage -> 02:22 ingress rule -> 02:28 runtime config change -> 02:36 nodes drained -> 02:45 error rate baseline restored to ~1-2%.

sanjay (runtime): remediation plan items: 1) immediate: keep ingress size limit for 24h, add request-body tokenization guard in fronted service. 2) short-term (48h): patch preprocessor to O(n) algorithm and add unit tests. 3) long-term: add synthetic load test for weird unicode-heavy prompts.

irina (cs): CS note: two customers impacted ~ 15-20 min of increased errors, majority recovered after ingress rule.

alex (oncall): thanks team. I'll post incident summary in #postmortems once we have the writeup. closing slack thread for active triage, handing to @mike for monitoring. :white_check_mark:

opsbot: incident INC-3981 status updated: monitoring.
